mcq.QUESTION_DESC: A function \(f(x)\) is said to be periodic if

mcq.OPT_1: It is single valued and finite in any interval.
mcq.OPT_2: It has atmost a finite number of discontinuities within the period.
mcq.OPT_3: It has finite number of discontinuities within the period.
mcq.OPT_4: It has infinite number of maxima and minima in any one period.

mcq.QUESTION_DESC: For \( f(x) = \sin(x) \) defined on \( (0, 2\pi) \), which statement is true about its Fourier coefficients?

sq.ANSWER: \( a_0 = \frac{1}{\pi} \int_0^{2\pi} f(x) dx --(1m)\\ a_n = \frac{1}{\pi} \int_0^{2\pi} f(x)\cos nx\, dx --(2m)\\ b_n = \frac{1}{\pi} \int_0^{2\pi} f(x)\sin nx\, dx --(2m) \)
sq.QUESTION_DESC: If  f(x) is a periodic function with period \(2\pi\), then the Fourier series of the function f(x) in the interval \([0,2\pi]\) is given by \( f(x) = \frac{a_0}{2} + \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \left[ a_n \cos nx + b_n \sin nx \right] \)

sq.ANSWER:
• It is a single valued and finite in any interval -- (1 m)
  • It has at at most a finite number of discontinuities with in the period -- (2 m)
  • It has finite number of maxima and minima in any one period --(2 m)
sq.QUESTION_DESC: A periodic function said to be satisfy Dirichlets Conditions if:

sq.ANSWER:
Upto the stepMarks

\(\text{The Fourier series is: } f(x) = \frac{a_0}{2} + \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} (a_n \cos nx + b_n \sin nx)\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{where coefficients are: } a_0 = \frac{1}{\pi} \int_0^{2\pi} f(x) dx\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{ } a_n = \frac{1}{\pi} \int_0^{2\pi} f(x) \cos nx \, dx, \quad n \ge 1\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{ } b_n = \frac{1}{\pi} \int_0^{2\pi} f(x) \sin nx \, dx, \quad n \ge 1\)

(2 Mark)
sq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{Define Fourier series of a function } f(x) \text{ of period } 2\pi \text{ in the interval } (0, 2\pi).\)

sq.ANSWER:
Upto the stepMarks

\(\text{1. } f(x) \text{ is periodic with period } 2\pi \text{ and bounded in } (0, 2\pi)\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{2. } f(x) \text{ is piecewise continuous with finite discontinuities}\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{3. } f(x) \text{ has finite number of maxima and minima in } (0, 2\pi)\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{If satisfied, series converges to } f(x) \text{ at continuity points, to average at discontinuities}\)

(2 Mark)
sq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{State Dirichlet's conditions for convergence of Fourier series.}\)

sq.ANSWER:
Upto the stepMarks

\(\text{Compute } a_0 = \frac{1}{\pi} \int_0^{2\pi} x dx = 2\pi\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{Compute } a_n = 0, \quad b_n = -\frac{2}{n}\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{Thus } x = \pi - 2\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{\sin nx}{n}\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{Put } x = \frac{\pi}{2}: \frac{\pi}{2} = \pi - 2(1 - \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{5} - \cdots) \Rightarrow 1 - \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{5} - \cdots = \frac{\pi}{4}\)

(3 Mark)
sq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{Find Fourier series for } f(x) = x \text{ in } 0 < x < 2\pi. \text{ Deduce } \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n}.\)

sq.ANSWER:
Upto the stepMarks

\(\text{At discontinuity } x = \alpha, \text{ series converges to average: } \frac{1}{2}[f(\alpha^-) + f(\alpha^+)]\)

(3 Mark)

\(\text{where } f(\alpha^-) = \lim_{h \to 0^+} f(\alpha - h), \quad f(\alpha^+) = \lim_{h \to 0^+} f(\alpha + h)\)

(3 Mark)

\(\text{This is Dirichlet's convergence theorem at discontinuities}\)

(2 Mark)
sq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{Explain convergence at discontinuity point in Fourier series.}\)

sq.ANSWER:
Upto the stepMarks

\(a_0 = \frac{1}{\pi} \int_0^{2\pi} e^{ax} dx = \frac{1}{a\pi}(e^{2a\pi} - 1)\)

(2 Mark)

\(a_n = \frac{1}{\pi} \int_0^{2\pi} e^{ax} \cos nx dx = \frac{a(e^{2a\pi} - 1)}{\pi(a^2 + n^2)}\)

(2 Mark)

\(b_n = \frac{1}{\pi} \int_0^{2\pi} e^{ax} \sin nx dx = \frac{-n(e^{2a\pi} - 1)}{\pi(a^2 + n^2)}\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{Series: } e^{ax} = \frac{e^{2a\pi} - 1}{\pi}[\frac{1}{2a} + \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} (\frac{a\cos nx}{a^2+n^2} - \frac{n\sin nx}{a^2+n^2})]\)

(2 Mark)
sq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{Find Fourier coefficients for } f(x) = e^{ax} \text{ in } (0, 2\pi).\)

lq.ANSWER: \(The \quad Fourier \quad series \quad of \quad a\quad function \quad in \quad the \quad interval \quad [0,2\pi]\\ f(x)=\frac{a_0}{2}+\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\left(a_n\cos nx + b_n\sin nx\right)\\ a_0 = \frac{1}{\pi}\int_{0}^{2\pi} x\, dx,\qquad\\ a_n = \frac{1}{\pi}\int_{0}^{2\pi} x \cos nx\, dx,\qquad\\ b_n = \frac{1}{\pi}\int_{0}^{2\pi} x \sin nx\, dx.\\ \textbf{1. Computation of $a_0$:} a_0 = \frac{1}{\pi}\int_{0}^{2\pi} x\,dx\\ = \frac{1}{\pi}\left[\frac{x^2}{2}\right]_{0}^{2\pi}\\ = \frac{1}{\pi}\left(\frac{4\pi^2}{2}\right)\\ = 2\pi.\\ \frac{a_0}{2} = \pi.\\ \textbf{2. Computation of $a_n$:}\\ a_n = \frac{1}{\pi}\int_{0}^{2\pi} x\cos nx\, dx.\\ Using \quad integration \quad by \quad parts \quad with \quad u=x, dv=\cos nx\,dx:\\ a_n=\frac{1}{\pi}\left[\frac{x\sin nx}{n} - \int \frac{\sin nx}{n}\,dx\right]_{0}^{2\pi}.\\ Since \sin(0)=0 and \sin(2n\pi)=0, this becomes\\ a_n = \frac{1}{\pi}\cdot \frac{1}{n^2}(\cos 2n\pi - \cos 0)=0.\\ Hence, a_n = 0.\\ \textbf{3. Computation of b_n:}\\ b_n = \frac{1}{\pi}\int_{0}^{2\pi} x\sin nx\, dx. \\ Using \quad integration \quad by \quad parts \quad with \quad u=x, dv=\sin nx\,dx\\ b_n = \frac{1}{\pi}\left[-\frac{x\cos nx}{n} + \int \frac{\cos nx}{n}\, dx\right]_{0}^{2\pi}.\\ Evaluate \quad at \quad limits:\\ b_n=\frac{1}{\pi}\left[-\frac{2\pi}{n}\right] = -\frac{2}{n}.\\ \textbf{Final Fourier Series:}\\ x = \pi - 2\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n}\sin(nx), \qquad 0<x<2\pi.\\ \)
lq.QUESTION_DESC: Expand the periodic function \(f(x)=x, 0<x<2\pi\) as a Fourier series in the interval \([0,2\pi]\)
Find the Fourier series for \(f(x)=x^2\) in the interval \((0,2\pi)\). Hence, deduce that \(\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{n^2} = \frac{\pi^2}{6}\).
Find the Fourier series for \(f(x)=e^{ax}\) in \((0,2\pi)\). Hence, find the sum of the series \(\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{a^2+n^2}\).
